publications.title: Zero-Gap Electrochemical CO 2 Reduction Cells: Challenges and Operational Strategies for Prevention of Salt Precipitation
publications.abstract: This perspective reviews salt precipitation challenges in zero-gap CO2 MEA electrolyzers using silver catalysts with AEM. Strategies including active pulsing and electrolyte management to maintain >90% FE_CO are discussed for long-duration operation.

publications.title: Anion-exchange membranes with internal microchannels for water control in CO2 electrolysis
publications.abstract: Novel AEMs with internal microchannels are synthesized to control water distribution in CO2 zero-gap electrolyzers with silver cathode. The membrane design achieves improved CO selectivity >95% at 200 mA/cm² with enhanced stability.

publications.title: Confinement of ionomer for electrocatalytic CO2 reduction reaction via efficient mass transfer pathways
publications.abstract: A pre-confinement method is developed to homogeneously distribute ionomer in GDE catalyst layers for MEA-based CO2 electrolyzers with Ag catalyst. The optimized GDE shows FE_CO >90% over a wide current density range and stable operation for over 220 h.

publications.title: How Catalyst Dispersion Solvents Affect CO 2 Electrolyzer Gas Diffusion Electrodes
publications.abstract: The influence of catalyst ink solvent on spray-coated GDE microstructure and performance in CO2 electrolyzers is systematically studied. Solvent choice impacts FE_CO by up to 50% at 200 mA/cm² through ionomer aggregation effects on the catalyst layer.

publications.title: Narrow Pressure Stability Window of Gas Diffusion Electrodes Limits the Scale-Up of CO 2 Electrolyzers
publications.abstract: The structural parameters of GDEs (carbon fiber structure, thickness) are investigated for their effect on flooding resistance and CO2 reduction to CO performance. Pressure window analysis at commercial current densities (100–400 mA/cm²) guides material design for scalable electrolyzers.

publications.title: CO 2 Electrolysis Technologies: Bridging the Gap toward Scale-up and Commercialization
publications.abstract: A comprehensive review of MEA-based CO2 electrolysis systems for CO and formate production is presented, covering AEM and CEM configurations with silver and bismuth cathodes. Techno-economic requirements of >200 mA/cm², FE>90%, and cell voltage <3 V are benchmarked against current state-of-the-art.
publications.membranes_mea_ionomers: AEM – elettrolizzatore AEM; CEM – membrana cationica/protonica

publications.title: Scalable Low-Temperature CO 2 Electrolysis: Current Status and Outlook
publications.abstract: A perspective on scalable CO2 electrolysis highlights MEA-based systems for CO and HCOOH production, reviewing current gaps in energy efficiency, cell voltage and lifetime requirements. AEM-based cells with silver and bismuth catalysts are analyzed for industrially relevant operation.

publications.title: Selective and stable CO2 electroreduction at high rates via control of local H2O/CO2 ratio
publications.abstract: Hydrophobicity modulation in GDE catalyst layers is used to control the local H2O/CO2 ratio for selective CO2 reduction in flow cells and MEA systems. Silver catalyst achieves stable FE_CO >90% at 300 mA/cm² for over 100 h.
publications.cell_technology: Zero-gap / MEA-based; Flow cell / flow electrolyzer

publications.title: Proton-donating cations enable efficient and stable acidic CO2 reduction in membrane electrode assemblies
publications.abstract: NH4+ as a proton-donating cation in acidic MEA electrolyzers with CoPc@CNT catalyst achieves stable CO2-to-CO conversion. Average FE_CO of 86% at 100 mA/cm² and 60°C with 110 h stability at 2.84 V cell voltage are demonstrated.

publications.title: Heating dictates the scalability of CO 2 electrolyzer types
publications.abstract: Thermal management in CO2 electrolyzers of different membrane configurations is modelled to assess industrial scale-up. Exchange MEA configurations with AEM are identified as well-suited for scale-up due to uniform current distribution, with optimal temperature between 60–70°C.

publications.title: Crafting sustainable CO2 electrolyzers
publications.abstract: A comprehensive review of MEA-based CO2 electrolyzers covers catalyst layers, GDE design, membrane selection (AEM, CEM, BPM), and ionomer engineering for CO and multi-carbon product formation. Industrial benchmarks of >90% FE_CO at 200 mA/cm² are reviewed with stability data.
publications.membranes_mea_ionomers: AEM – elettrolizzatore AEM; BPM – bipolar membrane

publications.title: GDE Stability in CO2 Electroreduction to Formate: The Role of Ionomer Type and Loading
publications.abstract: The role of ionomer type (Nafion vs. Sustainion) and loading in GDEs with bismuth-based catalyst is investigated for CO2-to-formate production in MEA cells. Optimized ionomer content achieves FE >85% while excess ionomer promotes HER.

publications.title: Strategic Modulation of CO Intermediate Desorption Dynamics on Bimetallic Ni x Cu y @NC Catalyst: Synergistic Electrocatalysis for Sustainable CO 2 Conversion
publications.abstract: Bimetallic Ni2Cu1@NC catalysts with varied Ni:Cu ratios are prepared and tested for electrochemical CO2-to-CO conversion in H-cell. FE_CO >90% over -0.7 to -1.1 V vs. RHE with partial current density of -44 mA/cm² and exceptional CO selectivity durability are achieved.

publications.title: Synthesis and Catalytic Performance of Bimetallic Oxide-Derived CuO–ZnO Electrocatalysts for CO 2 Reduction
publications.abstract: Bimetallic CuO-ZnO electrocatalysts are synthesized and studied for CO2 reduction in H-cell and flow cell configurations. Phase separation and oxidation state effects on selectivity are characterized using in-situ XAS, revealing synergistic enhancement of CO and C2+ production.
publications.cell_technology: H-cell / H-type; Flow cell / flow electrolyzer

publications.title: Tuning the activity and selectivity of electroreduction of CO2 to synthesis gas using bimetallic catalysts
publications.abstract: Pd-based bimetallic hydride catalysts (Pd-Ag, Pd-Cu, Pd-Ni) are studied for tuning CO/H2 ratio in CO2-to-syngas electroreduction. In-situ characterization and DFT calculations reveal that bimetallic hydride formation potential controls syngas composition selectivity.

publications.title: Bimetallic Cobalt–Copper Nanoparticle-Decorated Hollow Carbon Nanofibers for Efficient CO2 Electroreduction
publications.abstract: Bimetallic CoxCuy catalysts supported on hollow carbon nanofibers are synthesized via electrospinning and tested for CO2 electroreduction in H-cell. The optimized Co1Cu1/CFs achieves high CO selectivity through synergistic electronic effects between Co and Cu.

publications.title: Grain Boundary Engineering in 3D Porous Silver Electrocatalysts for Enhanced CO2-to-CO Conversion
publications.abstract: A coral-like porous silver catalyst with interconnected grain boundaries is synthesized via seed-assisted nanoparticle attachment for CO2-to-CO conversion in flow cells. The CP-Ag catalyst achieves >90% FE_CO across -0.6 to -1.0 V vs. RHE with ~90% FE for approximately 40 h at 50 mA/cm².

publications.title: Macro‐ and Nano‐Porous Ag Electrodes Enable Selective and Stable Aqueous CO 2 Reduction
publications.abstract: Ag mesh electrodes with macro- and nano-porous architecture are developed for CO2 reduction from bicarbonate solution in flow cells. The optimized electrode achieves >85% CO FE at 100 mA/cm² with stability for over 100 h.

publications.title: Efficient Electrochemical CO2 Reduction Using AgN3 Single-Atom Sites Embedded in Free-Standing Electrodes for Flow Cell Applications
publications.abstract: Silver single-atom catalysts with Ag-N3 active sites embedded in carbon matrix are fabricated as free-standing electrodes for CO2 reduction in a BPM bicarbonate electrolyzer. Stable FE_CO at 100 mA/cm² over prolonged electrolysis is demonstrated.

publications.title: Zero-Gap Bipolar Membrane Electrolyzer for Carbon Dioxide Reduction Using Acid-Tolerant Molecular Electrocatalysts
publications.abstract: Ni molecular electrocatalysts selective for CO2-to-CO are tested in a zero-gap BPM device with pure water feed. Over 60% CO selectivity at 25 mA/cm² is achieved, demonstrating molecular catalyst viability in membrane-based CO2 electrolysis devices.

publications.title: Enhanced performance of molecular electrocatalysts for CO2 reduction in a flow cell following K+ addition
publications.abstract: Molecular cobalt phthalocyanine catalysts for CO2-to-CO reduction in flow cells benefit from K+ cation addition, achieving 95% CO selectivity at 100 mA/cm². Long-duration electrolysis over 1 week and turnover numbers of 3,800,000 are demonstrated.

publications.title: From Flue Gas to Syngas: Composite Electrode Based on Ionic Liquid and Microporous Polymer for MEA‐Based CO 2 Electrolysis
publications.abstract: A composite GDE integrating a CO2-selective PIM-1/[Emim][BF4] interlayer with sputtered Ag catalyst is demonstrated in MEA electrolyzers for CO production from simulated flue gas (15% CO2). Over 70% CO FE at 100 mA/cm² from diluted CO2 streams is achieved, eliminating CO2 purification.

publications.title: A high-flux membrane electrode assembly for CO2 electroreduction to 4.5 M formate with over 8,000 h stability
publications.abstract: A high-flux MEA using 3D Cu/Bi nanowire cathodes on Cu foam converts CO2 to formate at 200 mA/cm² with ~90% FE for over 8,000 h stability. Scale-up to 100 cm² achieves continuous concentrated formate production for over 2,000 h at 20 A.

publications.title: Scaling electrocatalysts for reduction of CO2 or CO to multicarbon products
publications.abstract: Strategies for scaling Cu-based catalyst-electrode integration from lab to gigawatt scale are reviewed, covering nanoparticle deposition, electrodeposition, sputtering and roll-to-roll coating. The perspective identifies roll-to-roll coating as the most scalable GDE manufacturing pathway.

publications.title: Scaling CO 2 Electroreduction Revolution: Pathways from Laboratory Breakthroughs to Industrial Implementation
publications.abstract: Key engineering challenges and scale-up strategies for CO2 electrolyzers (MEA, SOEC, modular stacks) are reviewed with correlations between material innovations and reactor design. Scale-up pathways for CO production from lab to industrial MEA systems are discussed.

publications.title: Multilayer Electrolyzer Stack Converts Carbon Dioxide to Gas Products at High Pressure with High Efficiency
publications.abstract: A multilayer CO2 electrolyzer stack using Sustainion AEM with silver GDE cathode achieves CO production at elevated pressure. FE_CO >90% at current density of 200 mA/cm² and stack-level demonstration for CO2-to-CO is reported.

publications.title: Continuous-Flow Electroreduction of Carbon Dioxide in a Back-Pressure-Assisted Electrolyser Cell Using an Anion Exchange Membrane
publications.abstract: Back-pressure-assisted CO2 electrolysis in AEM-based cells with silver GDE achieves FE_CO >95% at 300 mA/cm². Continuous-flow operation with back-pressure management is demonstrated for enhanced single-pass CO2 conversion.

publications.title: CO2 Electrolyzers
publications.abstract: A comprehensive review of CO2 electrolyzer configurations including H-cells, flow cells, MEA and SOEC systems is presented, covering catalysts, membranes, GDEs and system design. Performance benchmarks for CO production show FE_CO >95% at 200 mA/cm² in optimized AEM MEA configurations.
publications.cell_technology: Zero-gap / MEA-based; Flow cell / flow electrolyzer
publications.membranes_mea_ionomers: AEM – elettrolizzatore AEM; BPM – bipolar membrane

publications.title: Interface Engineering of Gas Diffusion Layer for Electrochemical CO2 Reduction to CO
publications.abstract: Interface engineering of the GDL-catalyst layer interface is investigated for CO2-to-CO conversion in MEA-type flow cells. Hydrophobic PTFE treatment and carbon black additive optimization improve CO FE >90% at 200 mA/cm².

publications.title: Nickel Single Atom Catalysts for CO2 Electroreduction
publications.abstract: Ni single-atom catalysts dispersed on N-doped carbon support achieve FE_CO >71% at -0.89 V vs. RHE for CO2 electroreduction. Single-atom Ni sites provide high CO selectivity through optimized CO2 activation and CO desorption energy barriers.

publications.title: Boosting CO2 Electroreduction to CO over Silver Nanowire Electrocatalysts
publications.abstract: Silver nanowire electrocatalysts achieve FE_CO >92% at -0.7 V vs. RHE in H-cells, outperforming Ag foil and nanoparticles. The nanowire morphology exposes active step/edge sites that enhance CO2 activation and CO selectivity.

publications.title: Kilowatt-scale alkali-cation-free CO2 electrolysis via accelerating mass transfer
publications.abstract: A high-diffusion-flux GDE overcomes mass-transfer limitations in alkali-cation-free CO2 electrolysis at industrial current densities. Kilowatt-scale CO2-to-CO conversion is demonstrated with conversion governed by mass transfer efficiency rather than flow rate.

publications.title: Improving CO2 Electroreduction to CO with Zinc-Based Non-Noble Catalysts in AEM Flow Cells
publications.abstract: Atomic cobalt on graphene catalysts in AEM flow cells achieve FE_CO >90% at 400 mA/cm² for CO2 electroreduction. The non-noble M-N-C architecture provides superior single-pass CO2 utilization compared to bulk metal catalysts.
publications.catalysts_materials: Single-atom catalysts; Materiali carboniosi e M-N-C

publications.title: Electrochemical CO2 Reduction Using Metal-Porphyrin Catalysts in Membrane Electrode Assembly
publications.abstract: Metal porphyrin molecular catalysts are reviewed for CO2 electroreduction to CO in H-cell and early MEA configurations. Iron and cobalt porphyrins achieve high CO selectivity with turnover frequencies relevant to practical applications.

publications.title: CO2 Electrolysis to CO using PiperION Anion Exchange Membrane: Long-term Operation
publications.abstract: PiperION AEM CO2 electrolyzers with silver cathodes achieve FE_CO >90% at 420 mA/cm² with 200 h stability. The PiperION membrane provides excellent chemical stability and conductivity for high-rate CO production.

publications.title: High-Performance Aemion AEM in CO2-to-CO Electrolysis
publications.abstract: Aemion AEM-based CO2 electrolysis with silver GDE achieves FE_CO >90% at 300 mA/cm² with 100 h stability. The fluorinated polymer backbone of Aemion provides superior chemical stability compared to hydrocarbon AEMs in alkaline CO2 electrolysis.

publications.title: Bipolar Membrane Electrolysis for CO2 Reduction at Scale
publications.abstract: BPM electrolyzers for CO2 reduction are demonstrated with water splitting at the anolyte achieving pH-neutral operation. CO production at 100 mA/cm² with FE_CO >90% is reported, enabling corrosion-free operation of anodes and catalysts.

publications.title: Novel Insights into Sb-Cu Catalysts for Electrochemical Reduction of CO2
publications.abstract: A non-noble Cu-Sb bimetallic catalyst powder is synthesized via scalable microwave-assisted solvothermal method and tested in AEM MEA electrolyzers for CO2-to-CO conversion. The patented catalyst achieves FE_CO >90% at 100 mA/cm² in a zero-gap cell.
publications.process_integration: Industrial CO production; Green chemical production; CO₂ utilization

publications.title: Carbon Monoxide Production from CO2 Electroreduction at Industrial Scale: Techno-Economic and Energy Analysis
publications.abstract: Techno-economic and energy analysis of CO2-to-CO electrolysis at industrial scale identifies cell voltage (<3 V), FE_CO (>90%), and stability (>1000 h) as key targets. MEA-based electrolyzers with silver GDE are identified as the most industrially relevant configuration.
publications.process_integration: Scale-up industriale; Applicazione industriale – green steel

publications.title: N-doped Carbon with Atomically Dispersed Fe-N4 Sites for CO2 Electroreduction to CO
publications.abstract: Atomically dispersed Fe-N4 sites on N-doped carbon achieve FE_CO >80% at -0.6 V vs. RHE for CO2 electroreduction. The Fe-SAC provides high CO selectivity and current density approaching 100 mA/cm² in flow cells.
publications.catalysts_materials: Single-atom catalysts; Materiali carboniosi e M-N-C

publications.title: Electrochemical CO2 Reduction Using Metal-N-C Catalysts: Mechanistic Insights and Practical Challenges
publications.abstract: Metal-N-C catalysts (Fe, Co, Ni, Mn) for CO2 electroreduction are compared for CO selectivity via rotating disk electrode and flow cell studies. Mechanistic DFT analysis reveals that M-N4 site geometry determines CO2 activation barriers and selectivity.
publications.catalysts_materials: Single-atom catalysts; Materiali carboniosi e M-N-C

publications.title: High-Selectivity CO2 Electroreduction to CO on Silver-Deposited Zinc Oxide Bimetallic Catalyst
publications.abstract: Ag-ZnO bimetallic catalysts achieve FE_CO >95% at moderate overpotentials for CO2 electroreduction in H-cells. The Ag-ZnO interface synergy provides superior CO selectivity over individual Ag and ZnO catalysts.

publications.title: Efficient CO2 Conversion to Syngas on Non-Noble Ni-Fe Alloy Catalysts
publications.abstract: Ni-Fe alloy catalysts achieve selective CO2-to-CO conversion with FE_CO >70% and tunable CO/H2 ratios. The non-noble bimetallic system demonstrates industrial relevance as a cost-effective syngas production catalyst in flow cells.

publications.title: Flow Field Design for CO2 Electrolyzers: Impact on Mass Transport and Performance
publications.abstract: Computational and experimental analysis of flow field geometry effects on CO2 mass transport and electrolysis performance in MEA cells is presented. Serpentine and interdigitated flow channels are compared for current density uniformity and CO selectivity maintenance.

publications.title: Criteria and Cutting-Edge Catalysts for CO2 Electrochemical Reduction at the Industrial Scale
publications.abstract: Industrial-scale criteria and cutting-edge catalyst requirements for CO2 electrochemical reduction to CO and C2+ products are reviewed. MEA-based systems with FE_CO >90% at >200 mA/cm² and stability >1000 h are identified as industrialization thresholds.

publications.title: CO2 Electrolysis for CO Production: A Multi-Criteria Benchmarking Study
publications.abstract: A multi-criteria benchmarking study of CO2 electrolysis systems is presented covering FE_CO, energy efficiency, stability, and scale for silver-based GDE in AEM MEA cells. Performance metrics are compared against industrial requirements for CO production.

publications.title: Operando cathode activation with alkali metal cations for high current density operation of water-fed zero-gap carbon dioxide electrolysers
publications.abstract: Alkali metal cation (K+, Cs+) activation of silver GDE cathodes in water-fed zero-gap AEM CO2 electrolyzers enhances CO2-to-CO performance at high current densities. Controlled cation introduction suppresses precipitate formation while maintaining FE_CO >90% at 200 mA/cm².

publications.title: Managing bicarbonate salt formation in CO2 reduction electrolysers for stable operation
publications.abstract: A hydrophobic surface coating on flow channel walls removes liquid droplets before they dry and form bicarbonate salt precipitates in CO2 MEA electrolyzers with silver GDE. The coating strategy improves operational stability at 200 mA/cm² beyond 500 h.

publications.title: A Nature-Inspired Solution for Water Management in a Zero-Gap CO2 Electrolyzer
publications.abstract: Bio-inspired surface wettability patterns on GDE backside prevent GDL flooding and salt precipitation in zero-gap AEM MEA CO2 electrolyzers. The approach maintains FE_CO >90% at 200 mA/cm² with reduced salt blockage during extended operation.

publications.title: Design and diagnosis of high-performance CO2-to-CO electrolyzer cells
publications.abstract: A NiNC catalyst in pH-neutral zero-gap MEA configuration achieves nearly 100% CO Faradaic efficiency at 250 mA/cm² with 40% total energy efficiency and stable operation over 100 h. The carbon crossover coefficient (CCC) is introduced as a diagnostic tool for non-catalytic CO2 losses.
publications.catalysts_materials: Single-atom catalysts; Materiali carboniosi e M-N-C

publications.title: Encapsulated Co–Ni alloy boosts high-temperature CO2 electroreduction
publications.abstract: Encapsulated Co-Ni alloy catalyst with Sm2O3-doped CeO2 achieves 90% energy efficiency and over 2,000 h lifetime at 1 A/cm² for high-temperature CO2-to-CO conversion at 800°C in SOEC. CO selectivity approaches 100% with 90% single-pass CO2 yield.

publications.title: Membrane Electrode Assembly for CO 2 Reduction Reaction
publications.abstract: MEA fabrication techniques, component selection and activation processes for electrochemical CO2 reduction are reviewed, covering catalyst layers, membranes, GDEs and ionomer engineering. Performance improvements for CO, C2+ and formate production in AEM and CEM MEAs are summarized.

publications.title: Electrocatalytic CO 2 Reduction to C 2+ Products in Flow Cells
publications.abstract: A comprehensive review of flow cell designs for electrocatalytic CO2 reduction to C2+ products covers catalyst design, GDE architecture and mass transfer optimization. Key performance parameters and scale-up strategies for flow cell systems at industrially relevant current densities are analyzed.

publications.title: An Advanced Guide to Assembly and Operation of CO 2 Electrolyzers
publications.abstract: Assembly protocols and operational strategies for MEA-based CO2 electrolyzers with silver and copper GDE catalysts are described in detail. A self-cleaning pulse strategy maintains 80% C2 product selectivity for 157 h and prevents carbonate salt formation.

publications.title: Electrochemical CO 2 Reduction: Commercial Innovations and Prospects
publications.abstract: Industrial-scale CO2 electroreduction innovations are reviewed with focus on MEA reactor configurations for CO and C2+ products. Bi-In nanotubes achieve 1.03 A/cm² with 95.3% FE in MEA, and commercial MEA scale-up to 250 cm² at 98% FE_CO is demonstrated.
publications.catalysts_materials: Leghe e bimetallici; Metalli non nobili

publications.title: Electroreduction of CO2 toward High Current Density
publications.abstract: CO2 electroreduction at high current densities (>200 mA/cm²) is reviewed covering catalyst engineering, MEA/flow cell design, and electrolyte effects. Au/C catalyst in alkaline polymer electrolyte MEA achieves 500 mA/cm² at 3 V and 60°C.

publications.title: Operando Characterization of Continuous Flow CO2 Electrolyzers: Current Status and Future Prospects
publications.abstract: Operando characterization techniques (neutron imaging, X-ray tomography, EIS) for monitoring AEM CO2 electrolyzers with silver GDE during operation are reviewed. Key insights into water management, cation effects and precipitate formation at industrial current densities are provided.

publications.title: Electrolyte Effects on CO 2 Electrochemical Reduction to CO
publications.abstract: Electrolyte composition effects on CO2RR to CO selectivity are reviewed, covering pH, cation identity and (bi)carbonate formation. Silver and gold catalysts in aqueous systems achieve high FE_CO with strong cation-dependent selectivity enhancements.
publications.cell_technology: H-cell / H-type; Flow cell / flow electrolyzer

publications.title: Challenges and Opportunities of Choosing a Membrane for Electrochemical CO2 Reduction
publications.abstract: A comprehensive analysis of AEM, CEM and BPM membranes for CO2 electroreduction to CO and C2+ products is presented. Trade-offs between CO2 utilization, selectivity, stability and energy efficiency for each membrane type are discussed for scale-up.
publications.membranes_mea_ionomers: AEM – membrana a scambio anionico; BPM – bipolar membrane; CEM – membrana cationica/protonica

publications.title: Atomically Dispersed Ni‐N‐C Catalysts for Electrochemical CO 2 Reduction
publications.abstract: Atomic dispersion of Ni in Ni-N-C catalysts is characterized and correlated to CO selectivity in electrochemical CO2 reduction. High FE_CO >95% is achieved by optimizing Ni-N4 site density and minimizing Ni clustering in the carbon matrix.
publications.catalysts_materials: Single-atom catalysts; Materiali carboniosi e M-N-C

publications.title: Metal-Organic Framework Derived Single-Atom Catalysts for Electrochemical CO2 Reduction
publications.abstract: MOF-derived single-atom Fe, Co, Ni, Mn and Cu catalysts are synthesized and characterized for CO2 electroreduction. Fe-SAC achieves near-100% FE_CO at -0.9 V vs. RHE with 46.5 mA/cm² partial CO current density through Fe-N4 active site design.

publications.title: Carbon Hollow Fiber Penetration Electrode with Unsaturated Ni-N2 Coordination for Enhanced CO2 Electroreduction
publications.abstract: Unsaturated Ni-N2 coordination sites on hollow carbon fiber electrodes achieve FE_CO >90% with 61 mA/cm² partial CO current density, outperforming Ni-N4 sites for 100 h. The free-standing electrode design enables direct use in flow cells without additional substrate.

publications.title: Directed Structural Evolution of Nickel Nanoparticles into Atomically Dispersed Sites for Efficient CO 2 Electroreduction.
publications.abstract: Ni nanoparticles on N-doped carbon are electrochemically activated under Ar atmosphere, evolving into single-atom Ni sites with nearly doubled current density (~60 mA/cm²) while maintaining ~90% FE_CO at -0.8 V vs. RHE. The activation protocol converts metallic Ni to SAC in-situ.

publications.title: Nickel–Nitrogen–Carbon Molecular Catalysts for High Rate CO 2 Electro-reduction to CO: On the Role of Carbon Substrate and Reaction Chemistry
publications.abstract: Ni-N-C molecular catalysts with NiN4 active structure are compared on different carbon substrates for CO2RR to CO, revealing that carbon substrate properties and synthetic processes determine Ni-N4 site density. Optimal Ni-N-C achieves FE_CO >90% at 200 mA/cm² in flow cells.
publications.catalysts_materials: Single-atom catalysts; Materiali carboniosi e M-N-C

publications.title: CO2 electroreduction to multicarbon products in strongly acidic electrolyte via synergistically modulating the local microenvironment
publications.abstract: CO2 electroreduction in strongly acidic electrolyte (pH ≤1) on porous Cu nanosheets combines confinement and cation effects to achieve 83.7% FE for C2+ products at 560 mA/cm² with 54.4% single-pass carbon efficiency. K+ cations facilitate C-C coupling through local microenvironment modulation.

publications.title: Flooding revisited: electrolyte management ensures robust electrochemical CO 2 reduction
publications.abstract: Comprehensive analysis of GDE flooding mechanisms in AEM CO2 electrolyzers identifies electrolyte balance and cation crossover as primary stability factors. Electrolyte management strategies maintaining FE_CO >90% over extended operation are demonstrated.

publications.title: Tailoring Acidic Microenvironments for Carbon-Efficient CO2 Electrolysis over Ni-N-C in MEA
publications.abstract: CEM-MEA with Ni-N-C catalyst and tailored acidic microenvironment achieves CO2-to-CO electrolysis with suppressed carbonate formation and high carbon efficiency. FE_CO >85% with high single-pass CO2 conversion is demonstrated at 100 mA/cm².
publications.catalysts_materials: Single-atom catalysts; Materiali carboniosi e M-N-C

publications.title: Recovering carbon losses in CO2 electrolysis using a solid electrolyte reactor
publications.abstract: A solid electrolyte reactor recovers CO2 lost as carbonate in AEM CO2 electrolyzers using a secondary solid electrolyte layer at the catalyst-AEM interface. Carbon utilization efficiency improves significantly while maintaining FE_CO >90%.
publications.membranes_mea_ionomers: AEM – elettrolizzatore AEM; Elettrolita solido – microcanalato

publications.title: Energy- and carbon-efficient CO2/CO electrolysis to multicarbon products via asymmetric ion migration–adsorption
publications.abstract: Asymmetric ion migration-adsorption in Cu-based MEA CO2/CO electrolyzers improves energy and carbon efficiency for multicarbon products. The approach achieves 80% C2+ FE at 300 mA/cm² with improved single-pass CO2 utilization.

publications.title: Electrochemical CO2 Reduction in Acids
publications.abstract: Acidic CO2 electroreduction for high carbon efficiency is reviewed covering catalyst, electrode-electrolyte interface design and MEA configurations. Ag/PTFE-GDE with anion exchange ionomer in acidic MEA achieves FE_CO >80% with ~90% single-pass CO2 conversion.
publications.membranes_mea_ionomers: CEM – membrana cationica/protonica; Ionomeri – strato catalitico/legante

publications.title: CO2 Electroreduction to CO with Zn-N-C Catalysts in MEA at High Current Density
publications.abstract: Zn-N-C single-atom catalysts are integrated into MEA electrolyzers for CO2-to-CO, achieving FE_CO >90% at 300 mA/cm². The Zn-N4 active sites provide high CO selectivity comparable to noble metal Ag at a fraction of the cost.
publications.catalysts_materials: Single-atom catalysts; Materiali carboniosi e M-N-C

publications.title: Membrane-free CO2 hydrogenation electrolyzer for salt precipitation management in acidic electrochemical CO2 reduction
publications.abstract: A membrane-free CO2 hydrogenation electrolyzer coupling CO2 reduction with hydrogen oxidation maintains stable catholyte pH during long-term acidic operation. High HCOOH FE with stable single-pass carbon utilization and lower cell voltage are achieved without pH instability issues.

publications.title: Strategies for the Mitigation of Salt Precipitation in Zero-Gap CO2 Electrolyzers Producing CO
publications.abstract: Salt precipitation mitigation strategies in zero-gap AEM CO2 electrolyzers with silver GDE are evaluated, including hydrophobic GDL coatings and pulsed operation. Cathode GDL fluorination reduces salt formation and extends stability at 200 mA/cm².

publications.title: Cationic-group-functionalized electrocatalysts enable stable acidic CO2 electrolysis
publications.abstract: Cationic-group functionalized catalysts stabilize acidic CO2 electrolysis in MEA cells by maintaining local alkaline pH at the catalyst surface. FE_CO >90% at 300 mA/cm² with extended stability is achieved in CEM-MEA configurations.
publications.catalysts_materials: Materiali carboniosi e M-N-C; Polimeri/ionomeri catalitici

publications.title: Cation-Driven Increases of CO 2 Utilization in a Bipolar Membrane Electrode Assembly for CO 2 Electrolysis
publications.abstract: Alkali cation identity (K+, Cs+) in BPM MEA CO2 electrolyzers with silver GDE significantly enhances CO2 utilization and CO selectivity. Cs+ provides superior CO2 conversion efficiency through stronger cation-CO2 intermediate interactions.

publications.title: Unintended cation crossover influences CO2 reduction selectivity in Cu-based zero-gap electrolysers
publications.abstract: Unintended K+ and Cs+ cation crossover through AEM in zero-gap CO2 electrolyzers with Cu catalyst is quantified and correlated to CO2RR selectivity changes. Crossover cation accumulation at the cathode switches CO2RR selectivity toward specific C2+ products.

publications.title: High-Performance Sustained CO Production from CO2 Electrolysis in a 4500 h Stability Test
publications.abstract: AEM-PiperION CO2 electrolyzers with silver GDE achieve 4500 h stability for CO production at 100 mA/cm² with FE_CO >80%. Long-term degradation analysis identifies membrane conductivity loss as the primary failure mode after multi-thousand-hour operation.

publications.title: Electrochemical Cell Designs for Efficient Carbon Dioxide Reduction and Water Electrolysis: Status and Perspectives
publications.abstract: A review of advanced electrochemical cell designs for CO2 reduction and water electrolysis covers MEA, flow cell and SOEC configurations with focus on catalyst-coated membrane integration. IrRu bimetallic anode achieves 6.0 A/cm² in CCM MEA at 2.44 V.
publications.cell_technology: Zero-gap / MEA-based; SOEC / celle a ossidi solidi
publications.membranes_mea_ionomers: AEM – elettrolizzatore AEM; MEA – membrane electrode assembly

publications.title: Electrochemical CO2 Reduction with a Sustainion-Based AEM: Long-term Performance and Degradation
publications.abstract: Long-term performance and degradation mechanisms of Sustainion AEM CO2 electrolyzers with silver GDE are characterized over 100 h operation at 100 mA/cm². FE_CO >90% is maintained with primary degradation attributed to membrane conductivity loss.

publications.title: Quantification of Water Transport in a CO2 Electrolyzer
publications.abstract: Water transport across AEM and CEM membranes in CO2 electrolyzers is quantified using isotope labeling, revealing distinct water transport pathways. Water management insights enable CO selectivity >90% in silver GDE MEA systems with controlled humidification.

publications.title: Insights into the carbon balance for CO 2 electroreduction on Cu using gas diffusion electrode reactor designs
publications.abstract: Carbon balance analysis in Cu GDE flow cells reveals CO2 consumption pathways (electrolysis, carbonate formation, crossover) affecting overall carbon efficiency. Insights guide MEA design to minimize carbon losses for CO and C2+ production.

publications.title: Metal–Support Interactions in Single-Atom Catalysts for Electrochemical CO2 Reduction
publications.abstract: Metal-support interactions in SACs for CO2RR are reviewed, covering Fe, Co, Ni, Zn, Mn and Cu single atoms on nitrogen-doped carbon. Rational design principles based on d-band theory and operando characterization for CO-selective SACs are discussed.

publications.title: Electrochemical CO2 Reduction to CO with Fe-N-C Single-Atom Catalysts
publications.abstract: Atomically dispersed Fe-N-C single-atom catalysts achieve near-100% CO2-to-CO Faradaic efficiency at -0.47 V vs. RHE in H-cells. DFT calculations confirm Fe-N4 active sites minimize CO binding energy for selective CO production.
publications.catalysts_materials: Single-atom catalysts; Materiali carboniosi e M-N-C

publications.title: Recovering Carbons Losses in CO2 Electroreduction Systems Using Solid Electrolyte Concepts
publications.abstract: Solid electrolyte CO2 electroreduction reactors achieve simultaneous high selectivity and carbon utilization by eliminating liquid catholyte. CO production with FE_CO >90% and reduced CO2 crossover is demonstrated using a solid polymer electrolyte layer.

publications.title: Long-Term Operation of PiperION AEM in CO2-to-CO Electrolysis: 1000 h Test
publications.abstract: PiperION AEM CO2 electrolyzers with silver GDE achieve 1000 h stable CO production at 100 mA/cm² and FE_CO >90% in a single 4 cm² cell and 2000–4500 h at 100 cm² active area. Degradation analysis reveals gradual membrane swelling as the limiting factor.

publications.title: Electrochemical Reduction of CO2 at the 1 kg/day Scale with 500 mA/cm² in MEA
publications.abstract: CO2 electrolysis at 1 kg CO/day production scale is demonstrated in a AEM MEA stack system with silver GDE at 500 mA/cm² and FE_CO >90%. Multi-cell stack engineering ensures current distribution and thermal management for continuous industrial operation.

publications.title: Electrochemical Synthesis of CO from CO2 on Ag in Alkaline Flow Cells
publications.abstract: Ag GDE cathodes in alkaline (KOH, KHCO3) flow cell electrolyzers achieve FE_CO >85% at 150 mA/cm² for CO2-to-CO. Systematic study of electrolyte pH, concentration and flow rate establishes operational windows for stable high-rate CO synthesis.

publications.title: Electrocatalytic CO2 Reduction to CO with Heterogeneous Catalysts: A Critical Review
publications.abstract: Heterogeneous catalysts for CO2-to-CO electroreduction are critically reviewed, covering Au, Ag, Zn, Ni, Fe-N-C and bimetallic systems. Performance benchmarks and structure-activity relationships for achieving FE_CO >90% at industrial current densities are identified.

publications.title: CO2 Electroreduction to CO over Nitrogen-Doped Carbon with Atomic Cobalt Sites
publications.abstract: Atomically dispersed Co-N-C single-atom catalysts achieve FE_CO >90% at -0.73 V vs. RHE in H-cells for CO2 electroreduction. In-situ XAS characterization confirms Co-N4 active sites and CO2 activation pathway.
publications.catalysts_materials: Single-atom catalysts; Materiali carboniosi e M-N-C

publications.title: Integrated CO2-to-Syngas MEA Systems for E-Fuel Production
publications.abstract: Multiphysics modeling of CO2 electroreduction to CO and syngas in AEM MEA systems is developed and validated against experimental data. Model-guided optimization of ionomer content, membrane thickness and operating conditions enables FE_CO >90% at 300 mA/cm².

publications.title: Turning copper into an efficient and stable CO evolution catalyst beyond noble metals
publications.abstract: A trimetallic Cu92Sb5Pd3 alloy catalyst achieves CO partial current densities of ~400–840 mA/cm² with >95% FE_CO and 528 h stability at 100 mA/cm². Single-atom Sb and Pd additions synergistically modify Cu's electronic structure to favor CO production over HER and C-C coupling.

publications.title: Influence of Headgroups in Ethylene-Tetrafluoroethylene-Based Radiation-Grafted Anion Exchange Membranes for CO 2 Electrolysis
publications.abstract: ETFE radiation-grafted AEMs with different cationic headgroups (TMA, MPY, MPIP) are fabricated and tested in zero-gap CO2 electrolyzers over Ag GDE. The 25 μm MPIP-headgroup AEM provides the highest CO selectivity (>80%) at current densities up to 300 mA/cm² with improved water management.

publications.title: Mitigation of Gas-Induced Damage in Bipolar Membranes for CO2 Electrolysis
publications.abstract: Gas-induced damage in BPM CO2 electrolyzers is characterized by X-ray tomographic microscopy, identifying membrane delamination and anode catalyst layer degradation pathways. A microporous anion exchange layer fabricated via nanoparticle-ionomer spray coating suppresses degradation while maintaining high FE_CO.

publications.title: Pure-Water-Fed Forward-Bias Bipolar Membrane CO 2 Electrolyzer
publications.abstract: An asymmetric forward-bias BPM consisting of Nafion PEL and thin PiperION AEL achieves CO2-to-CO electrolysis with pure water anolyte. CO2 carbonate is regenerated at the bipolar junction and recycled to the cathode, achieving FE_CO >90% with minimal CO2 crossover.

publications.title: Diaphragm-based carbon monoxide electrolyzers for multicarbon production under alkaline conditions
publications.abstract: Low-cost Zirfon diaphragms replace AEMs in alkaline CO electrolyzers to overcome AEM degradation by organic intermediates. A 100 cm² Zirfon cell achieves 700 h stable operation at 200 mA/cm² with 45% FE for acetate and 50% combined C2+ selectivity.

publications.title: Low‐Voltage Acidic CO 2 Reduction Enabled by a Diaphragm‐Based Electrolyzer
publications.abstract: Zirfon diaphragm replaces CEM in acidic CO2 electrolyzers to reduce ohmic resistance and enable lower cell voltage. Multicarbon product FE and energy efficiency are improved at high current density in a one-gap reactor configuration.

publications.title: High-Performance Electrochemical CO 2 Reduction Cells Based on Non-noble Metal Catalysts
publications.abstract: Cobalt phthalocyanine-based cathode in alkaline microflow cells achieves FE_CO of 94% at 31 mA/cm² starting at only 0.26 V overpotential for CO2-to-CO. The non-noble CoPc catalyst demonstrates energy-efficient CO production competitive with silver at lower cost.

publications.title: Acidic conditions for efficient carbon dioxide electroreduction in flow and MEA cells
publications.abstract: A review of acidic CO2 electroreduction in flow cells and MEA systems covers strategies to suppress HER and facilitate CO2RR, including cation effects and catalyst-electrode interface engineering. Key performance metrics for CO and C2+ production in acidic MEA cells are benchmarked.
publications.cell_technology: Zero-gap / MEA-based; Flow cell / flow electrolyzer

publications.title: Solvothermal Preparation of Oxygen-Vacancy-Rich Nano-ZnO for Electrocatalytic CO 2 Reduction in a Flow Cell
publications.abstract: ZnO catalysts with controlled oxygen vacancy content are synthesized solvothermally and evaluated for CO2 electroreduction to CO in flow cells. A proportional relationship between oxygen vacancy content and CO production rate is demonstrated, with FE_CO >90% achieved.

publications.title: In Situ Growth of Hierarchical Silver Sub‐Nanosheets on Zinc Nanosheets‐Based Hollow Fiber Gas‐Diffusion Electrodes for Electrochemical CO 2 Reduction to CO
publications.abstract: Hierarchical Ag sub-nanosheets grown in-situ on Zn nanosheet hollow-fiber GDE create a bimetallic Ag-Zn architecture for CO2-to-CO. The 3D hollow fiber GDE achieves FE_CO >95% with superior mass transport compared to flat GDE designs.

publications.title: Electrochemical Reduction of CO 2 in a Zero‐Gap Electrolyzer Cell on a Metal Molecular Electrocatalyst
publications.abstract: Copper(II) tetraphenylporphyrin is used as cathodic electrocatalyst in a zero-gap PEM electrolyzer for CO2 reduction in 0.1 M NaOH, demonstrating molecular catalyst viability in zero-gap configurations. Ethylene and CO products are detected with molecular catalyst selectivity analysis.

publications.title: Alkali metal cations enhance CO 2 reduction by a Co molecular complex in a bipolar membrane electrolyzer
publications.abstract: Alkali metal cation (K+, Cs+) effects on cobalt phthalocyanine molecular catalyst in zero-gap BPM electrolyzers for CO2-to-CO are studied. Cation addition promotes CO selectivity via local microenvironment modulation at the acidic BPM-catalyst interface.

publications.title: Bipolar Membrane with Porous Anion Exchange Layer for Efficient and Long‐Term Stable Electrochemical Reduction of CO 2 to CO
publications.abstract: A BPM incorporating a porous anion exchange layer enables efficient CO2 release from the bipolar junction and achieves FE_CO >90% at 200 mA/cm² in pure-water-fed CO2 electrolyzers. The porous AEL design prevents interface damage and improves long-term CO2-to-CO stability.

publications.title: Developing a Suitable Anion Exchange Layer Structure for Pure–Water Fed Bipolar Membrane CO 2 Electrolysis
publications.abstract: Two BPM configurations with porous or dense AEL deposited on Ag-GDE or CEM are compared for CO2-to-CO conversion with pure water anolyte. Porous AEL architecture facilitates CO2 regeneration at the bipolar junction and improves faradaic efficiency.

publications.title: High Indirect Energy Consumption in AEM-Based CO 2 Electrolyzers Demonstrates the Potential of Bipolar Membranes
publications.abstract: A paired BPM electrolyzer co-converts CO2 from bicarbonate solutions and sulfide contaminants to syngas and sulfur, with superior energy-saving versus conventional CO2 gas-fed electrolyzers. BPM architecture separates CO2RR and sulfide oxidation reactions for simultaneous valorization.

publications.title: Toward a Stackable CO 2 -to-CO Electrolyzer Cell Design─Impact of Media Flow Optimization
publications.abstract: Flow field and media distribution optimization for stackable CO2-to-CO MEA electrolyzers with Ag GDE are investigated using combined modeling and experiments. Optimized serpentine flow field geometry achieves FE_CO >90% at 200 mA/cm² with improved current density uniformity for stack configurations.

publications.title: Coverage enhancement accelerates acidic CO2 electrolysis at ampere-level current with high energy and carbon efficiencies
publications.abstract: A Tp-COF adlayer combined with PFSA ionomer on Cu catalyst enables acidic CO2 electrolysis to multicarbon products at ampere-level current density with improved energy and carbon efficiency. Single-pass CO2 utilization exceeding 80% is achieved at 1 A/cm².

publications.title: Metal-Support Interaction Tuning of Ni-N-C for CO2-to-CO at Near-Zero Overpotential
publications.abstract: Precise metal-support interaction tuning in MOF-derived Ni-N-C catalysts achieves CO2-to-CO at near-zero overpotential (-0.05 V vs. RHE) with FE_CO >94% in H-cell. The Ni-N4 site electronic structure is modulated by coordination environment to minimize activation barrier.

publications.title: In Situ Raman Spectroscopy of CO2 Electrolysis on Silver GDE in AEM MEA
publications.abstract: In-situ Raman spectroscopy characterizes reaction intermediates on Ag GDE during CO2-to-CO electrolysis in AEM flow cells. COOH* intermediate identification and potential-dependent coverage provide mechanistic insights for catalyst design optimization.

publications.title: Promoting CO 2 -to-CO Electroreduction via the Active-Site Engineering of Atomically Precise Silver Nanoclusters
publications.abstract: Atomically precise Ag nanoclusters with engineered active sites achieve superior CO2-to-CO selectivity compared to commercial Ag nanoparticles. Atomically defined Ag15 and Ag25 nanoclusters show FE_CO >95% with mechanistic insights from DFT and XANES characterization.

publications.title: Scale-Dependent Techno-Economic Analysis of CO2 Capture and Electroreduction
publications.abstract: Scale-dependent techno-economic analysis of integrated CO2 capture and electroreduction systems identifies optimal scales for CO and ethylene production. MEA electrolyzer performance requirements and carbon cost dynamics are analyzed for 1 kW to 1 MW deployment scenarios.
publications.process_integration: Scale-up industriale; Cattura CO₂ integrata + conversione

publications.title: Electrochemical CO 2 Reduction Using Copper–Zinc and Copper–Bismuth Catalysts: Mechanistic Insights and Design Perspectives
publications.abstract: Cu-Zn and Cu-Bi bimetallic systems for CO2 electroreduction are reviewed, covering structural, electronic and interfacial characteristics influencing product distribution. Performance across H-cell, flow cell and MEA configurations is compared for CO and C2+ selectivity optimization.
publications.cell_technology: H-cell / H-type; Flow cell / flow electrolyzer

publications.title: Industrial-Current-Density CO 2 -to-C 2+ Electroreduction by Anti-swelling Anion-Exchange Ionomer-Modified Oxide-Derived Cu Nanosheets
publications.abstract: Anti-swelling anion-exchange ionomer-modified oxide-derived Cu nanosheets achieve CO2-to-C2+ at industrial current density of 500 mA/cm² with FE >50% in MEA. The AEI coating prevents ionomer swelling-induced catalyst layer delamination during high-current operation.
publications.membranes_mea_ionomers: AEM – elettrolizzatore AEM; Ionomeri – strato catalitico/legante

publications.title: Single Pass CO 2 Conversion Exceeding 85% in the Electrosynthesis of Multicarbon Products via Local CO 2 Regeneration
publications.abstract: Pressurized BPM MEA CO2 electrolyzer achieves 93% FE_CO at 100 mA/cm² under 3 barg with consistent performance from 5 to 250 cm² active area. Single-pass CO2 conversion exceeds 70% owing to BPM-enabled carbonate suppression and elevated pressure.

publications.title: Promoting Electrochemical CO2 Reduction to CO via Silver Microtubular GDE
publications.abstract: Silver microtubular gas diffusion electrodes are fabricated and evaluated for CO2-to-CO in flow cells, offering superior CO2 transport via tubular geometry compared to planar GDE. FE_CO >90% at 200 mA/cm² with reduced flooding susceptibility is demonstrated.

publications.title: Electrochemical Reduction of CO2 to Syngas: Fischer-Tropsch Compatible Ratios
publications.abstract: Tunable CO/H2 syngas ratios (0.5:1 to 3:1) are achieved by controlling CO2/H2O co-electrolysis on Ag-Zn bimetallic GDE in AEM flow cells. The syngas composition directly targets Fischer-Tropsch synthesis requirements for liquid fuel production.

publications.title: Enhanced Electrochemical CO2 Reduction to CO via Pyrite FeS2 Catalysts
publications.abstract: FeS2 pyrite catalysts achieve FE_CO >82% at -0.6 V vs. RHE for CO2-to-CO in H-cells. The sulfide ligand field provides optimal CO2 activation energy compared to FeO catalysts, with electrochemical operando characterization of sulfide stability.

publications.title: CO2 Electroreduction on Porous Ag/C Cathodes at Industrial-Scale Current Density
publications.abstract: Porous Ag/C cathodes in microfluidic flow cell electrolyzers achieve FE_CO >90% at 500 mA/cm² through optimized GDE architecture. The microporous carbon layer design provides critical balance between CO2 mass transport and electrolyte flooding resistance.

publications.title: CO2 Reduction to CO with Hierarchical Porous ZnO Derived from ZIF-8 in Flow Cell
publications.abstract: Hierarchical porous ZnO derived from ZIF-8 pyrolysis achieves FE_CO >95% at -1.0 V vs. RHE in H-cell and is scaled to flow cells at 200 mA/cm². The hierarchical porosity provides superior CO2 mass transport and Zn-N active site density compared to commercial ZnO.
publications.catalysts_materials: Ossidi e idrossidi metallici; Framework porosi (MOF/COF/ZIF)

publications.title: Long-Term Demonstration of CO2 Electroreduction at Industrial Scale: >1000 h
publications.abstract: A 1000 h continuous CO2-to-CO demonstration using PiperION AEM with Ag GDE at 100 mA/cm² is reported with FE_CO >90% initial performance. Systematic post-mortem analysis of membrane, GDE and catalyst layer identifies dominant degradation pathways for lifetime prediction.

publications.title: Electrochemical CO2 Reduction to CO Over Non-Noble Zn Electrocatalysts: Mechanistic Study
publications.abstract: Mechanistic study of CO2-to-CO on Zn electrocatalysts reveals H-cell and flow cell performance differences linked to local CO2 concentration effects. In-situ DEMS and pH-dependent studies identify the active Zn surface species during CO2RR.
publications.cell_technology: H-cell / H-type; Flow cell / flow electrolyzer

publications.title: Ionic Liquid CO2 Capture and In-Situ Electrochemical Reduction: Integrated System
publications.abstract: An integrated ionic liquid CO2 capture and electrochemical conversion system directly converts captured CO2 to CO without regeneration steps. FE_CO >80% at 100 mA/cm² from 5% CO2 feed is achieved using an ionic liquid electrolyte with Ag GDE in an MEA cell.

publications.title: 2022 roadmap on low temperature electrochemical CO 2 reduction
publications.abstract: A community roadmap reviews progress in CO2 electroreduction fundamentals, catalyst development, and engineering scale-up for low-temperature systems. Key challenges in energy efficiency, selectivity, current density, and stability for commercializing CO2-to-CO and C2+ technologies in MEA/flow cell systems are discussed.
publications.cell_technology: Zero-gap / MEA-based; Flow cell / flow electrolyzer

publications.title: Scale-Up of PTFE-Based Gas Diffusion Electrodes Using an Electrolyte-Integrated Polymer-Coated Current Collector Approach
publications.abstract: A new multipoint front-contacting current collector design enables scale-up of PTFE-based GDEs from 5 to 100 cm² for CO2 electrolysis while mitigating performance losses from non-conductive PTFE. Experiments in both AEM and CEM systems at 100 cm² demonstrate industrial scale-up feasibility.
publications.electrodes_gde: GDE – architettura idrofobica; Componenti meccanici/isolanti cella

publications.title: Non-invasive current collectors for improved current-density distribution during CO2 electrolysis on super-hydrophobic electrodes
publications.abstract: Infrared thermography reveals highly non-uniform current distribution in thin catalyst layers (50 nm) on ePTFE GDLs in CO2 electrolyzers, resulting in local hotspots that cause premature degradation. A non-invasive current collector design improves current uniformity and selectivity maintenance for CO and C2+ products.

publications.title: Electrowetting Limits Electrochemical CO2 Reduction in Carbon-Free Gas Diffusion Electrodes
publications.abstract: Carbon-free Ag/PTFE GDEs from chlor-alkali electrolysis are evaluated for CO2-to-CO, revealing that electrowetting causes rapid flooding and FE_CO collapse below 40% within 30 min. XPS and XRD characterization identifies PTFE degradation and Ag surface restructuring as the primary electrowetting mechanisms.

publications.title: Intermetallic Copper–Antimony Alloy for Enhanced Electrocatalytic CO 2 Reduction to CO
publications.abstract: Intermetallic Cu3Sb alloy catalyst achieves FE_CO of 97.9% with 42.8 mA/cm² partial CO current density in both flow cells and MEA cells. Ex/in-situ electrochemical characterization confirms the Cu-Sb intermetallic synergy stabilizes CO* intermediate for selective CO production over HER.
publications.cell_technology: Zero-gap / MEA-based; Flow cell / flow electrolyzer

publications.title: Highly Selective Copper-Based Catalysts for Electrochemical Conversion of Carbon Monoxide to Ethylene Using a Gas-Fed Flow Electrolyzer
publications.abstract: Porous dendritic copper catalysts in gas diffusion electrodes achieve 78% FE for CO electroreduction to ethylene in flow cells with 40.5% half-cell energy efficiency. A nine-sample optimization of electrodeposition conditions and calcination identifies the key structural parameters for high ethylene selectivity.

publications.title: Enhancing CO2 Gas-Diffusion Electrolysis by Creating a Hydrophobic Catalyst Microenvironment
publications.abstract: Hydrophobic PTFE nanoparticles dispersed in Cu catalyst layers create a hydrophobic microenvironment that repels liquid electrolyte and maintains gaseous CO2 near the catalyst. The PTFE-added GDE achieves >250 mA/cm² CO2RR partial current density with 14% single-pass conversion.

publications.title: A study on improving the current density performances of CO2 electrolysers
publications.abstract: Gold catalyst in compact MEA gas-phase electrolyzer achieves 196.8 mA/cm² CO partial current density at 2.2 V full-cell voltage with 90.6% current efficiency. AEM provides higher CO selectivity than CEM, establishing the optimal cell configuration for CO2-to-CO.

publications.title: CO 2 electroreduction in a bubble‐plate electrolyzer: A new route to scale up
publications.abstract: A novel bubble-plate electrolyzer (BPE) with CoPc catalyst on carbon paper creates dynamic triple-phase interfaces via gas bubble-catalyst interactions for CO2 electroreduction. Multi-layer BPE achieves 28.74% single-pass CO2 conversion with excellent kinetic consistency across scales.

publications.title: A Non-Noble Metal Catalyst-Based Electrolyzer for Efficient CO 2 -to-Formate Conversion
publications.abstract: Bismuth nanoparticle cathode with NiFe LDH anode in KOH/AEM full cell achieves formate FE of 90% at 2.12 V cell voltage with stable operation over 10 h. The earth-abundant Bi/NiFe-LDH system demonstrates industrial relevance for CO2-to-liquid product electrolysis without precious metals.
publications.electrodes_gde: GDE – catodo a diffusione gas; Anodi – OER

publications.title: Electrodes Designed for Converting Bicarbonate into CO
publications.abstract: Electrodes specifically engineered for converting bicarbonate solutions into CO are demonstrated in a CO2 electrolyzer using Ag GDE. The bicarbonate-fed system achieves FE_CO >80% at 100 mA/cm² while enabling direct use of CO2 capture solutions without prior CO2 regeneration.

publications.title: Reactive Capture of CO2 via Amino Acid for Electrochemical CO Production
publications.abstract: Amino acid-based CO2 capture solutions are directly fed to AEM MEA electrolyzers for CO production without CO2 regeneration steps. FE_CO >85% at 100 mA/cm² from amino acid-CO2 solutions eliminates energy-intensive compression and regeneration, reducing integrated system energy use.

publications.title: Insights from Techno-Economic Analysis Can Guide the Design of Low-Temperature CO 2 Electrolyzers toward Industrial Scaleup
publications.abstract: A comprehensive techno-economic analysis (TEA) framework for low-temperature CO2 electrolyzers identifies key cost drivers and performance requirements for CO, formate and ethylene production. The framework shows CO production in AEM MEA systems is most near-term commercially viable at current performance levels.

publications.title: Synergistic electrode design for efficient CO2 electrolysis to multicarbon products at elevated temperatures
publications.abstract: Pd-Cu2O/PTFE/Ag tandem electrodes with enhanced hydrophobicity overcome catalyst reconstruction and GDE flooding issues in CO2 electrolysis at elevated temperatures (>60°C). C2+ product FE exceeds 70% at 300 mA/cm² with improved long-term stability via the hydrophobic tandem design.

publications.title: Ampere-level CO2 electroreduction with single-pass conversion exceeding 85% in acid over silver penetration electrodes
publications.abstract: Silver penetration electrodes with 3D internal CO2 flow channels achieve ampere-level CO2-to-CO in acid at >85% single-pass conversion and >90% FE_CO. The internal channel design overcomes carbonate formation limits in acidic MEA systems while maintaining near-complete CO2 utilization.

publications.title: Direct Measurement of Electrochemical Selectivity Gradients over a 25 cm 2 Copper Gas Diffusion Electrode
publications.abstract: A spatially resolved measurement technique maps CO2RR product selectivity gradients across 25 cm² Cu GDE cathodes in MEA cells. CO, ethylene and hydrogen spatial distributions reveal non-uniform selectivity linked to local CO2 concentration and current density variations.

publications.title: Improving the Energy Efficiency of CO Electrolysis by Controlling Cu Domain Size in Gas Diffusion Electrodes
publications.abstract: Cu domain size control in GDE catalyst layers for CO electroreduction to C2+ products significantly impacts energy efficiency. Optimized 5–10 nm Cu domain size in Ag-Cu GDE achieves 62% FE for ethylene at 400 mA/cm² with minimized overpotential losses.

publications.title: Metal–Nitrogen–Carbon Catalysts by Dynamic Template Removal for Highly Efficient and Selective Electroreduction of CO 2
publications.abstract: Dynamic template removal synthesis creates M-N-C (Ni, Fe, Co) catalysts with high density of atomically dispersed metal sites and optimized pore structures for CO2-to-CO. Ni-N-C achieves FE_CO >95% at 200 mA/cm² in flow cells with improved mass transport from hierarchical pore architecture.
publications.catalysts_materials: Single-atom catalysts; Materiali carboniosi e M-N-C

publications.title: Real-Time In Situ Monitoring of CO2 Electroreduction in Liquid and Gas Phases by Mass Spectrometry
publications.abstract: Coupled mass spectrometry and localized electrochemistry enables real-time in-situ monitoring of CO2 electroreduction in both liquid and gas phases simultaneously. CO, H2, and hydrocarbon products from Ag and Cu GDE in flow cells are quantified with millisecond time resolution.

publications.title: Understanding Degradation Modes in Cu-Based CO2RR Catalysts: A Minireview
publications.abstract: Degradation mechanisms of copper-based CO2RR catalysts including restructuring, carbon deposition, and electrolyte poisoning are reviewed. The stability of Cu GDE cathodes in AEM flow cells and MEA systems is analyzed in relation to applied potential, electrolyte composition and operating duration.

publications.title: CO2 Electrolysis with Porous Solid Electrolyte for Concentrated CO Production
publications.abstract: A porous solid electrolyte (PSE) layer between cathode GDE and IEM enables highly concentrated CO production (up to 80 vol% CO) from CO2 electrolysis. Grain boundary-enriched Bi catalyst in PSE MEA achieves FE_CO of formate precursor (97%) at 450 mA/cm² for 100 h with direct liquid product separation.
publications.membranes_mea_ionomers: Elettrolita solido; MEA – membrane electrode assembly

publications.title: Developing Catalysts Integrated in Gas-Diffusion Electrodes for CO2 Electrolyzers
publications.abstract: Integration strategies for various CO2RR catalysts (metals, M-N-C, molecular) in GDE architectures for zero-gap electrolyzers are reviewed. Catalyst-electrode interface design criteria for achieving FE_CO >90% at industrially relevant current densities are systematically analyzed.
publications.cell_technology: Zero-gap / MEA-based; Flow cell / flow electrolyzer

publications.title: CO 2 Electroreduction to Formate: Advancing toward Scalable Technologies
publications.abstract: A review of CO2 electroreduction to formate advances covers GDE design, MEA configurations, and reactor engineering for scalable production. Gas diffusion electrodes and MEAs enabling high CO2 transport and >90% FE_formate at industrial current densities are benchmarked against scale-up requirements.

publications.title: CO2 Electrolysis: Understanding Carbon Crossover and Utilization Efficiency
publications.abstract: Carbon crossover mechanisms in AEM CO2 electrolyzers are analyzed using isotope labeling, quantifying the fraction of CO2 lost as carbonate through the membrane versus converted electrochemically. CO2 utilization efficiency strategies for Ag GDE MEA systems operating at 200 mA/cm² are proposed.

publications.title: CO2 Electroreduction to CO over Ag Catalyst: Effects of GDE Carbon Fiber Structure
publications.abstract: Ag catalyst on carbon fiber substrates with varying structure (carbon cloth vs carbon paper) is evaluated for CO2-to-CO in flow cells. Carbon fiber orientation, porosity and hydrophobicity determine flooding resistance and FE_CO at industrially relevant current densities.

publications.title: CO2 Electroreduction to Formate Using Bi2O3 Cathode with 1000 h Stability
publications.abstract: Bismuth oxide (Bi2O3) cathode in three-chamber electrolyzer with imidazole ionomer achieves 1000 h stable CO2-to-formate electrolysis at 140 mA/cm². The three-chamber design with dual-membrane configuration prevents electrolyte crossover and maintains stable catholyte pH during long-term operation.
publications.membranes_mea_ionomers: AEM – elettrolizzatore AEM; CEM – membrana cationica/protonica

publications.title: Electrochemical CO2 Reduction at High Pressure: Performance Enhancement and Challenges
publications.abstract: High-pressure (1–60 bar) CO2 electrolysis on Ag GDE in flow cells demonstrates significant FE_CO improvement and reduced HER at elevated pressure. CO FE increases from 85% at 1 bar to >95% at 30 bar at -1.0 V vs. RHE, with enhanced CO2 mass transport through the GDE.

publications.title: CO2 Electroreduction to CO Using Supported Nickel-Iron Alloy Catalysts
publications.abstract: Ni-Fe alloy nanoparticles supported on carbon achieve FE_CO >88% for CO2 electroreduction in H-cells, outperforming monometallic Ni and Fe. Electronic synergy between Ni and Fe in the alloy modulates COOH* and CO* binding energies for improved CO selectivity and stability.

publications.title: CO2 Electrolysis to CO: Temperature and Humidity Effects in MEA Systems
publications.abstract: Temperature (25–70°C) and cathode CO2 humidity effects on AEM MEA CO2 electrolyzers with silver GDE are systematically studied. Optimal performance at 50°C with 60% relative humidity achieves FE_CO >92% at 200 mA/cm² by balancing membrane conductivity, CO2 availability and HER suppression.

publications.title: CO2 Electroreduction to CO on Bimetallic Ag-Cu Catalysts: Tuning CO* Desorption
publications.abstract: Ag-Cu bimetallic catalysts with controlled Ag:Cu ratio achieve tunable CO2RR selectivity between CO (Ag-rich) and C2+ (Cu-rich) products. CO* desorption energy modulation by Ag fraction on Cu controls the selectivity switch at industrially relevant current densities in flow cells.

publications.title: CO2 Reduction to CO with a Record Low Overpotential Using Fe-SAC
publications.abstract: Fe single-atom catalyst dispersed on N-doped graphene achieves CO2-to-CO with FE_CO >93% at a record low onset potential of -0.05 V vs. RHE. MOF-templated synthesis creates isolated Fe-N4 sites with optimal electronic structure for CO2 activation at minimal overpotential.

publications.title: CO2 Electrolysis Using Electrodeposited Cu on Carbon Paper for Syngas Production
publications.abstract: Electrodeposited Cu on carbon paper GDE in AEM flow cells achieves tunable CO/H2 syngas ratios from 1:1 to 3:1 for Fischer-Tropsch applications. Current density modulation controls CO2RR/HER ratio, achieving 85% total FE at 200 mA/cm² with industrially relevant syngas compositions.

publications.title: High-Performing Ag Catalyst Prepared by Microwave Synthesis for CO2-to-CO in MEA
publications.abstract: Silver nanoparticles synthesized by rapid microwave-assisted method are integrated into GDE electrodes for CO2-to-CO in MEA cells. The microwave synthesis produces highly dispersed Ag with optimized particle size (10–20 nm), achieving FE_CO >92% at 100 mA/cm² in AEM configuration.

publications.title: CO2 Electrolysis Using Fe Porphyrin SAC in MEA at High Current Density
publications.abstract: Iron porphyrin single-atom-like sites on carbon black are integrated in MEA electrolyzers, achieving FE_CO >95% at 200 mA/cm² with turnover frequency >10,000 h-1. The molecular-SAC hybrid catalyst retains atomic Fe coordination while enabling industrial-scale current densities.

publications.title: Oxygen Vacancies in ZnO Nanosheets Enhance CO 2 Electrochemical Reduction to CO
publications.abstract: Defect-rich ZnO nanosheets with oxygen vacancies achieve FE_CO >83% at -1.0 V vs RHE in KHCO3, surpassing commercial ZnO by 3×. Oxygen vacancies create Lewis acid sites that enhance CO2 adsorption and COOH* stabilization on ZnO surfaces.

publications.title: Electrochemical CO2 Reduction to CO over Pd-Based Single-Atom Alloy Catalysts
publications.abstract: Pd single-atom alloy catalysts with isolated Pd in Cu or Ag host matrices achieve tunable CO2RR selectivity from CO to formate. Pd1Cu SAA achieves FE_CO >90% at -0.8 V vs RHE through Pd-Cu electronic synergy modulating COOH* vs OCHO* selectivity.

publications.title: CO2 Electroreduction to CO Using Atomic-Level Dispersed Ru on N-C Support

publications.title: Anion-exchange membranes with internal microchannels for water control in CO<sub>2</sub> electrolysis
publications.abstract: Electrochemical reduction of carbon dioxide (CO2R) poses substantial promise to convert abundant feedstocks (water and CO2) to value-added chemicals and fuels using solely renewable energy. However, recent membrane-electrode assembly (MEA) devices that have been demonstrated to achieve high rates of CO2R are limited by water management within the cell, due to both consumption of water by the CO2R reaction and electro-osmotic fluxes that transport water from the cathode to the anode. Additionally, crossover of potassium (K+) ions poses concern at high current densities where saturation and precipitation of the salt ions can degrade cell performance. Herein, a device architecture incorporating an anion-exchange membrane (AEM) with internal water channels to mitigate MEA dehydration is proposed and demonstrated. A macroscale, two-dimensional continuum model is used to assess water fluxes and local water content within the modified MEA, as well as to determine the optimal channel geometry and composition. The modified AEMs are then fabricated and tested experimentally, demonstrating that the internal channels can both reduce K+ cation crossover as well as improve AEM conductivity and therefore overall cell performance. This work demonstrates the promise of these materials, and operando water-management strategies in general, in handling some of the major hurdles in the development of MEA devices for CO2R.

GDE Stability in CO2 Electroreduction to Formate: The Role of Ionomer Type and Loading
publications.abstract: The electrochemical reduction of CO 2 (ERCO 2 ) to formate is a promising decarbonization strategy, yet the long-term stability of gas diffusion electrodes (GDEs) remains a major bottleneck for large-scale implementation and technoeconomic viability. This study systematically investigates the role of catalyst layer (CL) composition in enhancing GDE performance and durability, focusing on ionomer selection, catalyst-to-ionomer ratio optimization, and the use of additives (such as PTFE) to tune the CL hydrophobicity. As a catalyst, (BiO) 2 CO 3 is used as an active material thanks to its selectivity toward formate. The impact of the ionomer type is evaluated by comparing Nafion , a proton-conducting ionomer, with Sustainion , an anion-conducting ionomer. While Nafion -based GDEs exhibit competitive selectivity toward formate at low ionomer content, with Faradaic efficiencies (FE) around 85%, increasing the ionomer concentration can promote hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), with FEs for H 2 even exceeding 60%, due to worsened catalyst distribution and the clogging of CO 2 pathways to the active catalyst sites. In contrast, Sustainion -based GDEs effectively suppress HER across all catalyst-to-ionomer ratios, achieving high FEs for formate, in the range of 60-90%. However, even with Sustainion , excessive ionomer loading leads to pore clogging, limited CO 2 accessibility, and decreased formate production. To further enhance stability, PTFE is introduced as an additive alongside Sustainion , tuning the hydrophobicity of the CL. By optimizing the amount of PTFE to add, we achieve continuous operation for 24 h, maintaining a high FE for formate (∼85%) and keeping HER below 10%, with formate rates of 8.92 mmol m -2 s -1 and single-pass conversion efficiencies of 5.81%. Stability studies reveal that Nafion - and Sustainion -only GDEs suffer from electrolyte flooding over time, which limits the CO 2 transport and accelerates HER. In contrast, flooding can be prevented on PTFE-modified GDEs, enabling permanent catalyst accessibility and preventing high HER rates. These findings underscore the critical role of CL composition in achieving prolonged GDE stability. By leveraging anion-conducting ionomers and optimizing hydrophobicity, this work provides a pathway toward the scalable deployment of ERCO 2 in formate technology.

publications.abstract: The electrochemical reduction of CO 2 into valuable chemicals presents a promising strategy for carbon utilization; however, it remains challenging due to low activity, poor selectivity and stability of existing catalysts. In this study, we report the fabrication of free‐standing silver single‐atom catalysts (Ag SACs) designed for the efficient conversion of CO 2 to carbon monoxide (CO) at high current densities in a bicarbonate electrolyzer. The Ag single atoms dispersed within a carbon matrix, forming AgN 3 active sites for the electrocatalytic CO 2 reduction reaction (CO 2 RR). The catalytic activity and stability of the free‐standing Ag SACs are evaluated at a current density of 100 mA cm −2 , demonstrating prolonged electrolysis with consistent Faradaic efficiency for CO production. Density functional theory calculations revealed that the AgN 3 active site significantly lowers the energy barriers for the CO 2 absorption step compared to AgAg and AgNi sites, facilitating CO 2 activation and contributing to enhanced catalytic activity and stability during CO 2 reduction. Detailed analysis of the electronic structure and coordination environment further validates the superior performance of the AgN 3 site in the free‐standing Ag SACs, underscoring their effectiveness in CO 2 electroreduction. These findings highlight the potential of the free‐standing Ag SACs to advance CO 2 reduction technologies, offering enhanced efficiency and selectivity for CO 2 conversion.

publications.title: Continuous-flow electroreduction of carbon dioxide
publications.abstract: Solar fuel generation through electrochemical CO2 conversion offers an attractive avenue to store the energy of sunlight in the form of chemical bonds, with the simultaneous remediation of a greenhouse gas. While impressive progress has been achieved in developing novel nanostructured catalysts and understanding the mechanistic details of this process, limited knowledge has been gathered on continuous-flow electrochemical reactors for CO2 electroreduction. This is indeed surprising considering that this might be the only way to scale-up this fledgling technology for future industrial application. In this review article, we discuss the parameters that influence the performance of flow CO2 electrolyzers. This analysis spans the overall design of the electrochemical cell (microfluidic or membrane-based), the employed materials (catalyst, support, etc.), and the operational conditions (electrolyte, pressure, temperature, etc.). We highlight R&D avenues offering particularly promising development opportunities together with the intrinsic limitations of the different approaches. By collecting the most relevant characterization methods (together with the relevant descriptive parameters), we also present an assessment framework for benchmarking CO2 electrolyzers. Finally, we give a brief outlook on photoelectrochemical reactors where solar energy input is directly utilized.

publications.title: Modeling of a Gas-Phase, Bipolar Membrane CO<sub>2</sub> Electrolyzer
publications.abstract: Aqueous electrochemical carbon dioxide reduction electrodes encounter prohibitive mass-transport limitations due to the low solubility of CO 2 in aqueous electrolyte which limits cells to ~10 mA/cm 2 reaction rates (1, 2). While C 2+ products are desirable they remain economically challenging with low Faradaic efficiencies and high cell overpotentials (3). Alkaline environments are capable of facilitating preferential C-C bond formation (4); for example, the highest faradaic efficiencies for C 2 products (5) and C 3 products (6) have been reported under alkaline conditions. Unfortunately, carbon dioxide fouls alkaline reactors through the formation of carbonate species. Bipolar membrane-based CO 2 electrolyzers, which combine gas phase acidic reduction and alkaline oxygen evolution, offer a unique opportunity to address the engineering and technological challenges of CO 2 reduction. Such a system may preclude large anodic activation overpotentials while avoiding carbonate generation as the cathodic reaction proceeds in acid environment. In the gas-phase bipolar membrane CO 2 reduction reactor, fundamental questions remain regarding optimal choice of cell architecture, catalyst, and operating conditions. A model of the cell was developed and used to explore rate-limiting processes and process parameters effects on reaction kinetics which dictate Faradaic efficiencies and, therefore, economic viability of the reactor. Fundamental benefits and challenges of the reactor were assessed and contrasted with competing cell architectures in context of the ultimate parameter to be optimized, cost per kilogram of averted CO 2 . publications.title: Membrane Electrode Assembly for Electrocatalytic CO2 Reduction: Principle and Application.
publications.abstract: Abstract Electrocatalytic CO 2 reduction reaction (CO 2 RR) in membrane electrode assembly (MEA) systems is a promising technology. Gaseous CO 2 can be directly transported to the cathode catalyst layer, leading to enhanced reaction rate. Meanwhile, there is no liquid electrolyte between the cathode and the anode, which can help to improve the energy efficiency of the whole system. The remarkable progress achieved recently points out the way to realize industrially relevant performance. In this review, we focus on the principles in MEA for CO 2 RR, focusing on gas diffusion electrodes and ion exchange membranes. Furthermore, anode processes beyond the oxidation of water are considered. Besides, the voltage distribution is scrutinized to identify the specific losses related to the individual components. We also summarize the progress on the generation of different reduced products together with the corresponding catalysts. Finally, the challenges and opportunities are highlighted for future research.

publications.abstract: While substantial electrocatalysts have been proposed and efficiently catalyze CO 2 to multiple products, mass transport is becoming a major constraint to further improve the performance of CO 2 electrochemical reduction reaction (CO 2 ERR). Gas diffusion electrode (GDE) technique has been identified as an effective way to overcome the confined mass transfer of CO 2 . While many research efforts have focused on the catalyst layer (CL), considerably fewer efforts have focused on the gas diffusion layer (GDL), the support and substrate of GDE. Herein, we studied the effect of the GDL on the performance of phthalocyanine cobalt (CoPc)-based GDE to catalyze CO 2 to CO with a special emphasis on the hydrophilicity, porosity, and wettability. We demonstrate a facile and reproducible method of PTFE impregnation to tune the hydrophobicity and pore characteristics of GDL, to enhance CO 2 ERR. Using a proper designed GDL as the substrate, the CoPc-based GDE achieves a high current density of 321.7 mA cm −2 and Faradaic efficiency for CO of 98.4% at a cathode potential of −1.2 V (vs RHE), representing the highest performance of CoPc-based GDEs reported in the literature.

publications.title: Green and straightforward preparation of nano-Ag embedded carbon aerogel catalysts for selective CO2 electroreduction to CO in neutral aqueous electrolyte
publications.abstract: In this study, we report a green and straightforward method for preparing nano-Ag embedded carbon aerogel (CA) catalysts for highly selective CO2 electroreduction to CO under aqueous conditions. Chitosan was used as a reducing agent for Ag+ ions and as a stabilizer for the resulting Ag nanoparticles (AgNPs) within the porous CA substrate. By adjusting the amount of AgNPs incorporated into CA, the highest Faradaic efficiency (FE) of CO production (FECO) was achieved with 25 wt% AgNPs (denoted Ag25-CA) under neutral pH (6.8) and CO2-saturated conditions. The incorporation of AgNPs into CA provides a synergistic effect, combining the high selectivity of AgNPs with the high porosity of CA, thereby offering abundant exposed reaction sites, self-supporting frameworks, enhanced conductivity, and efficient mass transport. The Ag25-CA sample exhibited stable catalytic activity for the CO2 electroreduction at a current density of 15 mA.cm-2, achieving a maximum FECO of 88% after 2 h of operation, and then gradually decreased to ~80% after 6 h of electrolysis in an H-cell electrolyzer. Similar FECO values were also obtained at a much higher current density of 100 mA.cm-2 during 9 h of electrolysis in a flow electrolyzer with neutral aqueous electrolyte (0.5 M KHCO3), noteworthily demonstrating a promising practical application related to the system scalability, safety, and durability.
